name: Vector Pitch
tagline: 2,430 player-seasons from five international tournaments and six club league seasons, embedded in 24 dimensions where playing role — not league — sets the geometry.

insights.title: Role is the geometry, not fame
insights.body: The model is recorded as "PitchMTNN v1.1 (position SupCon)" and the vectors bear that out: the top-1 nearest neighbour of a player-season shares its position label 85.3% of the time. Mean cosine between same-position rows is 0.9244, against 0.7600 for different-position rows. Kevin De Bruyne's 2015/16 Manchester City vector sits 0.9098 from Mohamed Salah's Roma season, which is filed FWD, and only 0.8212 from Declan Rice at Euro 2024, which is filed MID.
insights.source: C:/Users/jcdav/vector-pitch/assets/pitch_mtnn_embeddings.json → model, players[].e_p, players[].pos (pairwise cosines computed over all rows)

insights.title: The league is essentially invisible
insights.body: Mean cosine between rows drawn from the same context is 0.8153; between rows from different contexts it is 0.8189 — the cross-context figure is marginally higher. Only 28.6% of top-1 nearest neighbours come from the same one of the 11 contexts. Messi's WC 2022 row is 0.9964 from Mbappé's WC 2022 but 0.9859 from his own 2018/19 Barcelona season, which ranks only 85th of 2,429 candidates.
insights.source: C:/Users/jcdav/vector-pitch/assets/pitch_mtnn_embeddings.json → contexts, players[].e_p, players[].context (cosines and ranks computed)

insights.title: The age axis is largely a team-quality ranking
insights.body: pitch_age_axis records corr(age, delivery) = -0.1671, while the delivery residual correlates 0.2626 with the leave-one-out teammate mean across 1,040 pairs. The file's own verdict on that comparison is "DOMINATES — the residual tracks team strength more strongly than age tracks delivery." Only 1,064 of 2,430 rows are scorable at all, and the labelled tails come to 208 P0 and 208 P1 with 624 left unlabelled.
insights.source: C:/Users/jcdav/vector-unified/data/pitch_age_axis.json → report.corr_age_delivery, report.team_strength_confound.{n_pairs, corr_residual_vs_teammate_mean, verdict}, report.rows_scorable, report.counts

insights.title: There is no free market prior for football, so age had to stand in
insights.body: The expectation-source audit resolved 1,538 of 1,833 distinct names (83.9%) using Wikidata SPARQL alone, with dob coverage at 83.9% and first-club-start at 80.2%. 115 names stayed ambiguous — "Paulinho" alone returned 18 candidate people, "Marquinhos" 13. Transfer fees and market values were rejected in advance because "No free source. Transfermarkt is the only real one and scraping it at corpus scale is neither polite nor reliable," and the file warns that age "is NOT the same construct as a draft slot."
insights.source: C:/Users/jcdav/vector-unified/data/pitch_expectation_sources.json → resolved_unambiguously, distinct_names, resolved_pct, field_coverage_pct_of_names, ambiguous_names, ambiguous_examples, rejected_in_advance, construct_warning

insights.title: Two "right-backs" the model refuses to pair
insights.body: Kyle Walker's Euro 2024 vector is 0.9977 from Thiago Silva's WC 2018 row and only 0.8276 from Achraf Hakimi at WC 2022, though all three carry the same DEF label. The same split shows up from the other side: van Dijk's WC 2022 row reaches 0.9992 to John Stones at Euro 2020 but falls to 0.8300 for Hakimi. Inside a single position label the spread is nearly 0.17 — wider than anything the league boundary produces.
insights.source: C:/Users/jcdav/vector-pitch/assets/pitch_mtnn_embeddings.json → players[].e_p for rows keyed on (name, context); cosines computed

game.prompt: Two real player-seasons, one anchor. Which one does Vector Pitch place closer to the anchor in its 24-dimensional space?
game.axis_label: Cosine similarity to the anchor (24-d e_p)
game.explainer: Every e_p vector in the file is unit length, so the score is the pure angle between two 24-dimensional role vectors — 1.0000 would mean identical direction.

caveat: Recorded verbatim in pitch_age_axis.json → report.team_strength_confound: "DOMINATES — the residual tracks team strength more strongly than age tracks delivery. Read P0/P1 as team-quality-contaminated." The per-position control that follows drives corr(residual, teammate mean) from 0.2626 to -0.0, but the same file flags that number as "ORTHOGONALITY BY CONSTRUCTION, not evidence — OLS residuals are orthogonal to their own predictors, so this check can no longer detect a residual team effect and must not be read as proving one is absent."
